title: ARIA attributes must be spelled correctly
summary: An attribute starting with aria- is not a real ARIA attribute, often a typo such as aria-pressd. Correct the name so it takes effect.
problem: An element has an attribute that begins with aria- but is not defined in WAI-ARIA, for example aria-pressd instead of aria-pressed. Browsers ignore unknown attributes, so the state or label you meant to expose never reaches assistive technology.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users miss the information the attribute was meant to carry, such as whether a button is on or off. The page looks and works correctly for sighted users, so the mistake is easy to ship unnoticed.
steps: Find the element and the misspelled attribute in the scan result.
Compare the name with the list of states and properties in the WAI-ARIA specification. Names are lowercase and use no hyphens beyond the aria- prefix, such as aria-labeledby and aria-describedby.
Correct the name and keep its value in sync with the visible state of the control.
If the attribute came from a framework or plugin, check whether it should be a data- attribute instead, since data-* names are not subject to this rule.
whyItMatters: A misspelled attribute fails silently, so a control can look finished while telling assistive technology nothing. This is a WCAG 4.1.2 Level A requirement (Name, Role, Value), the level that accessibility regulations and procurement requirements commonly build on.
howToCheck: Re-run the scan, then select the element in your browser's accessibility inspector and confirm the state or property you intended is listed.
